pool.text: The Hokkaido Development Commission headquarters established an administrative centre for the city.
The Hokkaidō Shrine was built in its current location as the Sapporo Shrine.
Edwin Dun came to establish sheep and cattle ranches in the area.
The Sapporo Breweries was founded as a major company and employer.
A railroad between Sapporo and Temiya, Otaru was laid during the ward renaming.
The red brick Hokkaidō government office building was constructed in an American-neo-baroque-style.
The Sapporo Municipal Bus System was started for the growing population.
The very first Sapporo Snow Festival was held in the city.
Kouraku Ramen Meitengai in Susukino became an alley lined with many miso ramen restaurants.
The Peace Pagoda stupa was built halfway up Mount Moiwa to commemorate peace.
The Sapporo Symphony Orchestra was officially founded to enrich local music.
A ceremony was held to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the foundation.
The Sapporo Municipal Subway system was inaugurated, becoming the fourth in Japan.
Opera singer Maria Callas gave her last public performance at the Hokkaido Koseinenkin Kaikan.
The Sapporo Municipal Subway expanded when the Tōzai line started operation.
The Tōhō line opened alongside the New Chitose Airport development.
The Pacific Music Festival started as an annual cultural event in the city.
The Yosakoi Sōran Festival began as a major annual event in the city.
A professional football club named Consadole Sapporo was established.
The Sapporo Concert Hall Kitara opened its doors to music lovers.
